- When sentiment is high (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true), model often overshoots; cap next-period forecast at 1–2% below peak.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model consistently overpredicts mid-to-late period (days 15–30) in 30-day horizon; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% for days 15–25.
- When sentiment alternates sharply (e.g., 0.67 → 0.00 → 1.00), model misreads momentum; align forecast with sentiment swing direction, not trend.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 75→72→70), model often holds too long; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 3–5 days after reversal.
- Avoid forecasting based on 30-day history alone; weight recent 7–10 days more heavily if sentiment is volatile.
